memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The total amount of the gold from the wave offering used for all the work on the sanctuary was 29 talents and 730 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel. The silver obtained from those of the community who were counted in the census was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel." - Exod 38:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Numbers. Exact weights, measured by a fixed standard — "the sanctuary shekel."

That last phrase matters. There was an agreed measure that did not shift according to who was weighing. Everyone was assessed by the same standard.

Scripture repeatedly insists on honest weights. Differing weights and differing measures are both detestable to the Lord (Prov 20:10). We instinctively know why: a merchant who uses one weight when buying and another when selling is a thief with good manners.

But there is a deeper application. We are all tempted to use two standards — a generous one for ourselves and a strict one for everyone else. We explain our own failures by our circumstances and judge others by their actions.

Jesus addressed this directly: with the measure you use, it will be measured to you (Matt 7:2). And He told us to remove the plank from our own eye first.

There is one sanctuary shekel. God's standard does not bend for any of us — which is exactly why we need Christ, who met that standard on our behalf.

Weigh yourself by the same measure you use for others.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you judge yourself by intentions and others by actions?
2. Where are you using two different standards?
3. What would change if you applied God's measure to yourself first?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, remove the double standards from my heart. Measure me by Your truth, and clothe me in Christ's righteousness. Amen.
